title: DeepSeek Search and Fetch API: Pricing and Reliability
summary: DeepSeek search and fetch is available for your automation. Learn when it released and what operational responsibilities come with using it.
body_markdown:
## What Activepieces has already shipped for DeepSeek search and fetch


### The shipped support and its date


Whoever owns the workflow should know one difference before it pages them:[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/deepseek) lets you use DeepSeek as one of the models behind a workflow, not as a dedicated search-and-fetch action.


Activepieces works with any major model or your own provider key, and you can swap one for another without rebuilding the workflow, so DeepSeek can be used that way. The DeepSeek integration,` @activepieces/piece-deepseek` , is listed in the integration catalog.


What that means in practice: the model step can change without the rest of the workflow being rebuilt around it.


That support doesn't say that live web search or page fetch is exposed as its own step. Treat those capabilities as unconfirmed on the Activepieces side until you see them in the integration's actions.


If the search or fetch action you need isn't there, the gap doesn't have to wait on anyone's release schedule.


Activepieces can generate an integration with AI and add it privately to your own instance, so a DeepSeek search or fetch step becomes something you build rather than something you request.


### Connecting it in a workflow today


We haven't run this ourselves, so there are no test results here, only the route the product gives you.


In the flow builder, add a step and the Select Step panel opens on the right. Type the name of what you need into its search field and filter by All, Core or App Actions.


The screenshot shows that panel searched for "sheet", returning spreadsheet integrations, on a canvas holding an Every Hour trigger, an Ask ChatGPT action and an End node.


Search for "deepseek" the same way and the integration should appear if your instance has it. Swapping it in for the Ask ChatGPT step is the obvious first experiment.


Next comes the ownership question: who holds the DeepSeek API key, and who gets the failure alert when a call returns nothing.
